prompt: Before deciding whether to take the breath test, did the defendant ask to contact anyone? Select all that apply.
options: A relative or friend (not an attorney)

prompt: If a relative or friend was requested, what was the stated or apparent purpose of that request?
options: To get advice on whether to take the test, or what to do (defense-related)
Purely personal — e.g. arranging bail, notifying family, emotional support — no defense-related purpose apparent
Request was denied outright — no opportunity to contact anyone was given
An opportunity was given, but the defendant was not able to communicate privately
An opportunity was given, but not within a reasonable time given the circumstances (e.g. the person could have arrived or advised further, but wasn't given the time to)
A reasonable opportunity to contact and consult was given

prompt: Roughly what was the timeline — when was the request made, when was contact made (if any), and when was the test administered?
Was a breath test actually administered (as opposed to refused, or not administered at all)?
Did the officer clearly and expressly advise the defendant of the right to an independent chemical test?
options: No advisement of the right to an independent test was given at all
An advisement was given, but it did not clearly and expressly explain the right or how to exercise it
A clear and express advisement was given

prompt: Did the advisement explain only one type of independent test (e.g. only blood), without mentioning that other types might exist?
Was there anything that may have prevented the defendant from actually understanding the advisement, even if it was properly given?
options: Language barrier — advisement was given only in a language the defendant did not adequately understand
Intoxication level so severe the defendant could not knowingly and intelligently understand the advisement
Other comprehension barrier (e.g. cognitive impairment, disability)
